output.name: Óllun

anatomy.part: lantern at the top of the mast, pointing north toward home
belly of the sail, the brightest point of the canvas
lower curve of the sail, where the foot bellies out
mast foot, stepped into the deck amidships
bow lamp at the forward end of the deck
prow tip, angled down toward the south

output.myth: Óllun was a sailor who asked the wind where it stopped. He took his boat south, past the last of the kelp, until the water went smooth and dark and the stars were strange. Aun had gone that way before him and had not come back, and Óllun thought he might find him. Tavo the Gale laughed at the bow and would not push him further. So Óllun reached the edge of the Unflown, looked over, and turned his boat around. He had not found the end of the wind, only the place where it stopped being kind. Hesk, who keeps count, wrote his name once on the reel and said nothing else. His lantern still hangs on the mast, pointing home. His hull faces the wrong way, south, where lost things go. Sil looks for him every month and never finds the boat. My grandmother says that if you fly a kite on a still night and feel nothing pull, that is Óllun turning around.
output.verse:
Turned boat, lamp to north,
mast to home, keel to the south,
the sea let him go.
